good: Scenario sheet. Task: a one-paragraph summary an agent acts on without opening the ticket; user: the support agent; good-answer rules: every action item traces to a ticket line, no commitment the ticket does not contain, the same language as the ticket, refund and SLA amounts quoted verbatim. Hazard list, one line each, sized to this task: a hallucinated commitment such as last month's invented refund promise; a missing citation to the ticket line; the wrong language; incomplete action items. Limits block, written before any scoring dimension: at least 80% of golden rows graded good, because below that agents stop trusting the summary; zero hallucinated commitments, since one honoured refund costs more than the feature saves; a citation present on 100% of summaries so that every action can be checked; at most 5% of outputs asking a question instead of summarising, because the agent has no way to answer. Decision rule: ship at 80% good or better; a single invented commitment or citation blocks the release regardless of the pass rate. Golden set: 24 rows, six per language across EN, PT, DE and ES, real traces first, including the real refund incident labelled fail with its one-line reason and three more real failures; the file is versioned with the prompt. Validation: run the refund incident through the rubric first and tighten the rules if it passes. Verification: two people re-grade a sample of about thirty judge-scored cases blind against a disagreement threshold we set before the run, and a rate above it means we investigate the judge before trusting its scores. Synthetic rows are practice; real traces decide the release.
bad: Eval plan: grade 50 sample summaries on accuracy, helpfulness, tone, safety and style, and ship when the average score is above 4 out of 5. We will generate synthetic tickets to test with, and agents can report problems after launch.
